# lnurlcash-conformance

Test vectors, an adversarial mock mint, and a grader for LNURLcash (LUD-25).
MIT. Use these when implementing LNURLcash in ANY language.

npm install --save-dev lnurlcash-conformance

## Vectors

Plain JSON in vectors/, loadable from any language, listed in
vectors/index.json:

signature.json       offline verification, both recovery-id orderings
derivation.json      deterministic note secrets from a BIP39 seed
bech32.json          LUD-01 encoding
url-admission.json   which URLs may be fetched (https, or http to loopback/.onion)
input-resolution.json bech32, LUD-17, Lightning Address, bare domain
note-url.json        parsing/building note URLs
fees.json            fee advertisement, application, gross-up, overflow case
bolt11.json          amount extraction, invoice equality
callbacks.json       exact query per operation
responses.json       classifying replies incl. ambiguous outcomes
withdraw-info.json   the informational GET
pay-request.json     minting, LUD-11, LUD-21
payment-request.json lnurlcashreq1: asking another holder for value
settle-for-value.json the decision table for taking a note as payment
lifecycle.json       behavioural scenarios
threat-suite.json    transport/exposure scorecard, options vs attacks (non-normative)

## Mock mint

import {createMockMint} from 'lnurlcash-conformance/mock-mint'
const mint = await createMockMint({dropAfterMutation: true})
mint.state.creditNote(k1, 21000)   // then drive your client at mint.url
await mint.close()

Misbehaviour flags: dropAfterMutation, unconfirmedMutation, malformedJson,
echoWrongK1, lieAboutValue, signatureLayout=leading, signatures=false,
serverGeneratedSecrets, meltNeverSettles, meltAlwaysFails, slowMs, sunset,
baseFeeMsat, feePpm, verify=false, withdrawLinkForm=lnurlw (the lnurlw://
spelling of withdrawLink; default is the plain https://, as lnurl-mint).

Optional extensions, all outside LUD-25, all absent or off by default:
name, description, contact, tosUrl, motd, version (mint info on
/.well-known/lnurlw/<user>); fees (emitted there whenever a fee is
configured); stats=true (serves GET /stats: at, outstandingMsat,
outstandingNotes, pendingMsat, pendingMelts, oldestPendingMeltAgeSecs,
localBalanceMsat, coverage, reconciledAt) with localBalanceMsat to set
what the node claims to hold; previousPrivateKey and previousPubkeys
(signing-key rotation), plus signWithPreviousKey to issue every note under
the old key. state.creditNote(k1, amount, {previousKey: true}) signs one.

CLI: npx lnurlcash-mock-mint --port=8899  (nothing is payable)

## Grader

npx lnurlcash-conform mint@example.com                        read-only
npx lnurlcash-conform mint@example.com --note=<url> --spend   full, burns the note

Exit code non-zero on any failure. The optional extensions are graded
softly: a mint publishing none of them loses nothing, a published field of
the wrong shape warns, and a signature under a key the mint publishes in
previousPubkeys is accepted as its own.

## The signature scheme, canonically

note_id = hex(sha256(k1))
message = "LNURLcash:" + amount_msat + ":" + note_id
digest  = sha256(sha256("Lightning Signed Message:" + message))
sig     = 65 bytes, r || s || recovery_id (wire format)
pubkey  = 33-byte compressed, hex

Recover from digest with NO further hashing (prehash off). Verifiers MUST
also accept recovery_id || r || s. Library layouts differ:
@noble recid-leading; coincurve trailing; Rust secp256k1 64-byte compact +
RecoveryId; Go btcec recid+27 leading.

## Payment requests, canonically

lnurlcashreq1 || base64url(JCS(request)), no padding. JCS is RFC 8785:
keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, no whitespace, non-ASCII left alone.
Canonical so two wallets building the same request produce the same
string. request = {v: 1, id: 16 hex, amount: whole sat as a DECIMAL
STRING, currency: "sat", methodDetails: {mints: [host, ...]}, to?: npub or
name@domain, memo?: string, expires?: unix seconds}. The payer sends
amount * 1000 msat exactly. Refusal reasons are enumerated in the vector.

## Settling a note for value, in order

host in acceptedMints -> ask the mint (spent/pending surface here) ->
signature when required -> value >= price -> rotate. The rotate is LAST:
it is the settlement and the double-spend check in one call, and a server
that rotates before comparing the amount has taken the money and refused
the request. Full table in settle-for-value.json.

## Fee arithmetic

apply(gross, fee) = max(0, gross - base - floor(gross*ppm/1e6))
Compute the proportional term as floor(gross/1e6)*ppm + floor((gross%1e6)*ppm/1e6):
a direct multiply overflows u64 at realistic amounts (2.1e15 msat * 999999 ppm).
grossUp(net, fee) = the SMALLEST gross where apply(gross) == net. Use binary
search; apply is non-decreasing with steps of 0 or 1. An estimate-then-walk
implementation is unbounded at 999999 ppm and returns non-minimal answers.
